{{Short description|Polish mathematician}}
'''Ewa Maria Kubicka''' is a Polish mathematician interested in [[graph theory]] and [[actuarial science]].{{r|cv}} She is known for introducing the concept of the [[sum coloring|chromatic sum]] of a graph, the minimum possible sum when the vertices are labeled by [[natural number]]s with no two adjacent vertices having equal labels.{{r|scg}}

Kubicka studied mathematics at [[Wrocław University of Science and Technology]] beginning in 1974, and earned a master's degree there in 1979. She came to [[Western Michigan University]] for graduate study, earning both a master's degree in computer science and a Ph.D. in mathematics in 1989.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''The Chromatic Sum and Efficient Tree Algorithms'', was supervised by Allen J. Schwenk.{{r|mgp}} She became an assistant professor at [[Emory University]] and then, in 1990, moved to the [[University of Louisville]], where she has been a full professor since 2004.{{r|cv}} At Louisville, she directs the actuarial program and is undergraduate advisor for mathematics.{{r|ul}}

She is known for having an [[erdős number]] of one.{{r|mp}}{{r|en}}
